sheets.why: A lies like a heavy skirt: soft folds, a pointed front panel resting on the ground, and the bag sitting on the coat. B is a stiff flat boxy sheet with hard straight edges, and its bag is crumpled.
B's coat settles over the hip and the bag stays whole. A's skirt bunches into a boxy slab and the bag is folded and crushed.
A's coat stays close and drapes over the bent leg. B pulls the coat into a lifted ridge and leaves the trousers' flat cut ends showing beside the coat.
A's panel lies along the thigh like hanging cloth. B throws a flap up into a pointed wing.
A lets the coat fall to the ground beside the raised leg. B sticks a panel up as a spike and shows a flat trouser cut in the top view.
Both let the leg rise through the coat front. Neither lets the cloth fall away from the lifted leg or lie on the ground. Column 1 reads slightly more natural in B, column 3 in A.
B's side view (column 1) drapes the cloth in a heavy lump, not a standing tent. Both rows still have a standing flap in the top view and a detached trouser tube.

stands: Raised-leg poses (5 and 6): in both rows a coat flap stands up against gravity (a fin or hood), and in pose 6 B it hoods the lantern; neither way yet drapes cloth away from a lifted thigh.
One way leaves the lying leg's flat trouser end visibly floating above the coat in the top view: pose_2 B, pose_3 B, pose_5 B, pose_6 A.
The same way crumples and folds the orange bag under a stiff coat panel: pose_0 B, pose_1 A, pose_3 B, pose_5 B, pose_6 A.
The same way makes boxy, faceted, board-like coat sheets: pose_0 B, pose_1 A.
Pointed hem tip to the ground in the other way's front panel: pose_3 A, pose_5 A, mild in pose_2 A.
Dark trouser rim showing beside the coat in the top view: pose_1 A.
Pose_4 shows no fault in either row; it is the clean sheet.
struck: Pose_4 flaws attributed to B by cloth, guide and player (spike, floating tube, cut end, crumpled bag): not in the pictures; they belong to pose_3 B.
Pose_4 A 'hem spike to ground' (cloth, guide, player): hem is rounded; the spike is in pose_3 A and pose_5 A.
Cloth's 'cloth through body' at the lantern in pose_5: the boot and leg are in front of the lantern, nothing penetrates.
Player's pose_6 preference for A: the floating tube is in A, not B; B is the truer row.
Player's pose_2 A 'bag crushed': A's bag is whole.
Player's pose_3 A 'gap' at tube end and pose_6 A 'dark spike below leg': not seen.
Guide's pose_0 B 'tube gap': tubes meet the coat.
referee.missed: ["Pose_5: the detached flat tube end in the top view in the less true row, and its crumpled bag, were missed by cloth and player, who called the sheet the same.","Pose_4: both rows are the same, so nothing separates them.","Pose_6: the lying leg's cut end is the detached-leg fault, not the raised leg."]
